Northern Illinois Huskies.previous_hc_experience: None. The Coaching Carousel records that the 43-year-old Rob Harley has never been a head coach, was the defensive coordinator last season under Thomas Hammock, is a Pat Narduzzi disciple, and was a GA under Narduzzi and Mark Dantonio for two years.
Northern Illinois Huskies.dc: Not addressed by name for 2026. Harley himself ran the unit last season.
Northern Illinois Huskies.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide records a new offense.
Northern Illinois Huskies.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator, the role Harley vacated on being named interim head coach.
Northern Illinois Huskies.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Northern Illinois Huskies.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records a new offense.
Northern Illinois Huskies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide notes Harley ran the unit last season so there is familiarity.
Northern Illinois Huskies.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide describes how bleak the position looked two weeks before publication — Brady Davidson and Jalen Macon having combined to complete under 50% for four touchdowns and three interceptions — before Taron Dickens was released by North Carolina over academic issues in mid-July and Northern Illinois moved, which it calls a huge win.
Northern Illinois Huskies.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 6 returning starters — a total of 0.
Northern Illinois Huskies.staff_turnover: Complete and unplanned. The guide records Thomas Hammock leaving in February for an NFL job with the Seahawks and Rob Harley being named interim, and the Coaching Carousel adds the timing problem — the transfer portal opened up when Hammock left in February.
Northern Illinois Huskies.prior_school: Not addressed for the staff beyond Harley's own lineage under Pat Narduzzi and Mark Dantonio. On the roster the guide records Taron Dickens as a one-time North Carolina commit and former Western Carolina quarterback.
Northern Illinois Huskies.portal_recruiting: Immense turnover, especially on defense, with the guide noting Harley added bodies but that none come from the Power Four and most are FCS or junior college transfers.
Northern Illinois Huskies.vsin_assessment: A situation both parts of the guide call weird, with the coach's status the central problem. The Coaching Carousel says Harley finds himself in a weird situation to say the least with the travel, games at elevation, and the portal opening when Hammock left in February. The team pages' summary word is chaos: they list a defense building from the ground up, Harley's own apparent lame-duck status, and a conference transition, then read the situation as Harley being in place to take the lumps before ultimately being replaced — concluding this could get ugly quickly. It leaves the defensive question open between Harley doing his best work rebuilding mid-flight and this becoming one of the country's worst defenses.
Northern Illinois Huskies.strengths: A head coach who ran this defense last season so there is scheme familiarity, a coaching lineage under Pat Narduzzi and Mark Dantonio, and a late portal quarterback addition the guide calls a huge win — 271 of 365 for 3,508 yards with 38 touchdowns to two interceptions at Western Carolina, including an NCAA record 46 consecutive completions in a game.
Northern Illinois Huskies.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with six returning starters and no returning starters at all on defense, the top 14 tacklers from 2025 gone, an interim head coach the guide treats as a lame duck, a head-coaching departure that hit as the portal opened, and a simultaneous conference transition with travel and elevation.
Northern Illinois Huskies.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked framing is a question about a team projected to win three or four games.
Northern Illinois Huskies.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens on the strangeness of the realignment itself — if Sacramento State being in the MAC wasn't enough of a mind-eff, Northern Illinois is a member of the retooled Mountain West. He sets out the sequence: Harley was the DC last season under Thomas Hammock and is the interim HC for this season after Hammock took a job with the Seahawks. He records the lineage — Harley is a Pat Narduzzi disciple and was also a GA under Narduzzi and Mark Dantonio for two years — then states the constraints plainly: the 43-year-old has never been a head coach, and finds himself in a weird situation to say the least with the travel, games at elevation, and the transfer portal opening up when Hammock left in February.

San Jose State Spartans.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
San Jose State Spartans.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
San Jose State Spartans.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
San Jose State Spartans.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide records Craig Stutzmann's Spread and Shred offense taking the conference by storm two seasons ago before fizzling in 2025, and identifies a genuine pattern within it — a previously unheralded receiver erupting, with Nick Nash producing 1,382 yards and 16 touchdowns in year one and Danny Scudero catching 88 passes for 1,297 yards and 10 touchdowns last season.
San Jose State Spartans.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
San Jose State Spartans.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split beyond the scheme name.
San Jose State Spartans.qb_development: Addressed as scheme fit rather than a record. The guide judges Luke Weaver — a seasoned and well-travelled redshirt senior who worked his way up from Modesto Junior College and started two Hawaii games in place of the injured Micah Alejado — likely gives San Jose State the best chance specifically in this system.
San Jose State Spartans.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 0 for 3 returning starters, totalling 7.
San Jose State Spartans.staff_turnover: The guide credits staff continuity as one of Ken Niumatalolo's assets while the Stability Score table records the defensive coordinator position changing.
San Jose State Spartans.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Luke Weaver from Hawaii, Robert McDaniel as a one-time UCLA transfer, and Anthony Ivey as a former four-star from Penn State.
San Jose State Spartans.portal_recruiting: The programme's defining problem this year. Per Phil Steele, San Jose State lost 24 starters to the portal and brought in two, with only three full-time starters returning from a three-win team. The guide notes some former Power Four transfers are involved while adding the realistic caveat that all are making this move for a reason.
San Jose State Spartans.vsin_assessment: Credit for a previous rebuild, with the reason it may not repeat named precisely. The guide credits Niumatalolo's fantastic first season in a similar situation while identifying the difference: that came with an ingenious offense that surprised the league, and in his third season many opponents have now seen the tendencies. Its conclusion credits him as a good coach with staff continuity while judging that he would need one of the best coaching jobs of a long career to get this group into the mix.
San Jose State Spartans.strengths: A head coach who has already rebuilt this roster once, staff continuity, a distinctive named offense with a documented record of producing an unheralded 1,300-yard receiver in each of its two seasons, and a former four-star receiver arriving into that system.
San Jose State Spartans.concerns: Only three returning starters with 24 lost to the portal and two added, receiver, defensive line and defensive back all losing every starter, a new defensive coordinator, and the guide's own point that opponents have now seen the offense's tendencies.
San Jose State Spartans.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

UNLV Rebels.dc: Paul Guenther, who joined last March as associate head coach and safeties coach before being thrust into the coordinator role when Zach Arnett resigned in April.
UNLV Rebels.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
UNLV Rebels.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator, consistent with Guenther having taken the role during last season.
UNLV Rebels.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
UNLV Rebels.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
UNLV Rebels.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, and the guide reports a reason offered for its absence: people around the programme say Guenther could not install his own scheme, producing poor results — 104th nationally in opponent EPA per play, 6.4 yards per play and 5.2 yards per carry allowed.
UNLV Rebels.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
UNLV Rebels.qb_development: The guide's central coaching argument for this programme. It records that UNLV has not returned a starting quarterback since Doug Brumfield in 2023, with five different starters over that span, yet still accumulated 30 wins and three title game appearances, and draws the precedent directly: Dan Mullen took in Anthony Colandrea last season, made him Mountain West Offensive Player of the Year and sent him to Nebraska for a payday. It concludes that the co-favorite's season rests on Mullen working his magic at the position again.
UNLV Rebels.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes again. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 10.
UNLV Rebels.staff_turnover: Not addressed for 2026. The guide's staffing history is last season's disruption — Zach Arnett resigning in April and Guenther being thrust into the role.
UNLV Rebels.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Jackson Arnold from Auburn and Alex Orji from Michigan.
UNLV Rebels.portal_recruiting: The roster model. The guide records another roster built on transfers, with both running back depth and the receiver room as a whole consisting of transfers expected to carry large loads.
UNLV Rebels.vsin_assessment: Delivery credited, repeatability doubted, and one explanation explicitly rejected. The guide says Mullen delivered in year one but must do it again with another roster built on transfers, and sets the stakes for the coach: he keeps a cool exterior, but failing to win the Mountain West, let alone missing the title game, would be a colossal failure. Its pointed defensive conclusion is that with a full offseason there is no excuse to lean on regarding preparation, and it adds separately that it finds the staff's explanation for last season's defensive effort hard to buy.
UNLV Rebels.strengths: A head coach with a documented record of turning portal quarterbacks into conference Offensive Player of the Year, 30 wins and three title game appearances across a span with five different starting quarterbacks, full staff continuity, a defensive coordinator now with a full offseason, and a first-team all-conference running back who averaged 7.2 yards per carry.
UNLV Rebels.concerns: Only six returning starters on another transfer-built roster, no returning quarterback for a fourth straight year with the presumed starter unproven and the backup coming off a catastrophic leg injury, all three top receivers gone, a defense ranked 104th in opponent EPA per play with four starters back, and an explanation for that the guide says it finds hard to buy.
UNLV Rebels.betting: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. Its logic is explicitly about the coaching pattern: UNLV cannot keep sustaining the quarterback success of the last three seasons, with this depth chart looking more flawed, and the guide asks what happens if Jackson Arnold struggles and loses the job while Alex Orji is not the same athlete.

UTEP Miners.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
UTEP Miners.dc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 260–261) record Kyle Beyer taking over as coordinator having been an analyst last season, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
UTEP Miners.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
UTEP Miners.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide quantifies what must be turned around: an offense that ranked 131st in EPA per play and 129th in success rate.
UTEP Miners.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records a quietly strong campaign — 14th nationally in opponent EPA per play, 20th in success rate, 97th percentile in explosive play rate allowed and 94th percentile in late-down success rate.
UTEP Miners.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records 116 rushing yards per game at 3.7 per carry, with the programme not averaging more than 3.9 since 2022.
UTEP Miners.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Scotty Walden naming EJ Colson the starter in May, traces his path through UCF and Incarnate Word, and frames the task as Herculean — turning around a bottom-five offense without the top four rushers and top seven receivers.
UTEP Miners.continuity: Head coach returns and the defensive coordinator column prints returning points, but the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 6 returning starters, totalling 7. The team pages describe the defensive coordinator position differently — see the conflicts field.
UTEP Miners.staff_turnover: The team pages record Kyle Beyer taking over the defense after a season as an analyst.
UTEP Miners.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records EJ Colson from Incarnate Word by way of UCF, Brian Williams from the SWAC, Jaymon Lamb from North Texas and Tavorus Jones from Missouri.
UTEP Miners.portal_recruiting: Credited as competent hole-filling. The guide says the staff has plugged holes decently through the portal, names Missouri transfer Tavorus Jones the crown jewel at running back, and records line help in an all-conference SWAC left guard and a North Texas right tackle.
UTEP Miners.vsin_assessment: Modest optimism grounded in one strong unit. The guide says UTEP was a sneaky solid defense at times last season and that the staff has plugged holes decently through the portal, sees enough on offense to be somewhat optimistic about climbing out of the national cellar, and expects the defense to improve once conference play begins — with a strong chance of an above-average Mountain West unit.
UTEP Miners.strengths: A defense that ranked 14th nationally in opponent EPA per play with a productive returning linebacker and two returning defensive backs, competent portal work including a former four-star running back from Missouri and two line additions, and a quarterback named the starter in May with a 70.9% completion season behind him.
UTEP Miners.concerns: A 2-10 season, only six returning starters, an offense ranked 131st in EPA per play losing the top four rushers and top seven receivers, no returning offensive line starters, and a rushing attack that has not averaged more than 3.9 yards per carry since 2022.
UTEP Miners.betting: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins. The coaching-linked reasoning is that there is enough on offense to be somewhat optimistic, with much depending on EJ Colson, and that the defense could also improve once conference play begins.
UTEP Miners.conflicts: The guide states the defensive coordinator position two ways. The team pages (pp. 260–261) record Kyle Beyer taking over as coordinator having served as an analyst last season, while the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator. Both are reproduced as printed and neither is corrected.

Wyoming Cowboys.oc: Christian Taylor, most recently an offensive advisor with the Buffalo Bills and William & Mary's coordinator from 2020 to 2023.
Wyoming Cowboys.oc_status: New — the guide records Jay Sawvel hiring Taylor, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Wyoming Cowboys.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Wyoming Cowboys.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Wyoming Cowboys.offensive_scheme: Not named, but described by its previous output. The guide details what Taylor's William & Mary offenses did well — generating explosive runs, using backs out of the backfield, and leading the country in passing efficiency — and says all of it will be needed. It also notes this is reportedly a strong tight end group, which matters in the new scheme.
Wyoming Cowboys.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide describes the defense as having a strong foundation.
Wyoming Cowboys.run_pass: Addressed through the incoming scheme's characteristics — explosive runs and backs used out of the backfield.
Wyoming Cowboys.personnel: Addressed in part: the guide notes the strong tight end group matters in the new scheme.
Wyoming Cowboys.qb_development: Addressed as pre-existing familiarity rather than a development record. Sawvel brought in one of Taylor's former William & Mary recruits, quarterback Tyler Hughes, a dual threat who totalled 3,000 passing and rushing yards with 31 touchdowns and already knows the system.
Wyoming Cowboys.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 0 for 5 returning starters, totalling 7.
Wyoming Cowboys.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive side, and presented as the head coach's fix for his central problem: he addressed the biggest problem by hiring an offensive mind.
Wyoming Cowboys.prior_school: William & Mary, twice over — Taylor coordinated there from 2020 to 2023 and recruited Tyler Hughes there. The Buffalo Bills were Taylor's most recent stop.
Wyoming Cowboys.portal_recruiting: Mixed but stable. The guide notes Wyoming lost talent to the portal while most of the roster has been in the programme, and supplies a supporting statistic from Phil Steele: although returning starters are few, 77.2% of the roster is homegrown.
Wyoming Cowboys.vsin_assessment: A disappointing tenure with a specific, identified fix. The guide acknowledges the difficulty of following a legend given Craig Bohl's success, then judges Sawvel's tenure disappointing even in that context: seven wins total, with one of the conference's worst offenses. It is blunt that the offense has collapsed under him — despite nine returning starters last season Wyoming averaged 16 points and 315 yards per game, ranking 128th nationally in EPA per play and 124th in success rate. It notes he is in year three of a five-year contract, that the first two were not great, and calls this his best chance at a winning record.
Wyoming Cowboys.strengths: A coordinator hire with a documented record of explosive runs, backfield receiving and the country's leading passing efficiency, a quarterback the coordinator recruited who already knows the system, defensive-coordinator continuity with what the guide calls a strong foundation, a returning leading rusher behind two returning linemen with 41 career starts, and a roster that is 77.2% homegrown.
Wyoming Cowboys.concerns: Seven wins in two seasons, an offense ranked 128th in EPA per play, only five returning starters, the top four receivers gone, and mounting pressure on the head coach in year three of a five-year contract.
Wyoming Cowboys.betting: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, with the upside case stated first and framed entirely through the coaching change: if Tyler Hughes and coordinator Christian Taylor are the match they look on paper, the offense could stun the conference and let Sawvel focus on a defense with a strong foundation.
